items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Nottingham – James Nottingham – James Nottingham and me, we were trumpeters.

ctx.x: [introduces himself again, but the distortion is worse than before. His opening statement is barely audible and the subsequent question, evidently on Charlie Barnet’s band, is inaudible.]

We did – the only that I know of that the band ever did, we did at Town Hall. I think that was in ’47. We did Charleston Alley and Gal from Joe’s and tunes of that sort. I don’t recall any other particular things that we did. We were on the road for a bunch of the time. Neal Hefti wrote for the band, and we had – at one point, Doc Severinsen was in the band. No particularly unusual things happened, except – oh, I know one thing that did happen, in the form of relations with bigotry. We were leaving Washington,…

colored people in here.” I said, “You’re not allowed to serve colored people in here?” “No, we’re not.” When the band heard them say that – Doc Severinsen was in the band – they all got angry. They took all of the pies and stuff out of the tray and threw them behind the counter up against the mirror, the back wall mirror. They told them, said, “Okay. Just give our bill to Bilbo.”
